home.intro2: Mostly Swift and SwiftUI, and lately some C#.
home.about.p1: I mostly build for the Mac, because it's what I use every day. Occasionally Windows and the web, too.

project.swiftZip.title: Swift Zip Manager
project.swiftZip.body1: Handles ZIP, TAR, GZ, 7Z, and RAR, including encrypted archives. Browse contents before extracting, drag files from Finder, and pull out individual files without unpacking everything.
project.swiftZip.body2: Built entirely in SwiftUI. Currently in beta, heading toward 1.0.
project.runprocess.title: RunProcess
project.runprocess.body1: A native macOS menu bar app that opens a floating command window on a global hotkey. Real-time output with 8/16/256-color and 24-bit truecolor ANSI rendering, Tab completion for aliases and file paths, frecency-ranked command history with ⌘R fuzzy search, drag-and-drop paths, custom executable paths, and secure sudo handling.
project.runprocess.body2: RunProcess also has a browser demo, hosted on Process WebHub alongside a ProcessSH demo — same interfaces, rebuilt in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
project.runprocess.body3: Three appearance modes — None, Frosted Glass, and Liquid Glass (macOS 26+) — let it match the rest of your screen. Session mode keeps a persistent shell alive between launches, so cd and export persist across commands.
project.runprocess.body4: Process WebHub is a static site with working recreations of both desktops: draggable windows, simulated shells, switchable window materials, and custom wallpapers. No install required.
project.processSH.title: ProcessSH
project.processSH.body1: A lightweight Windows app that wraps PowerShell 7 in a Spotlight-style floating window. Opens on a global hotkey, lives in the system tray, and stays out of the taskbar.
project.processSH.body2: Acrylic backdrop, Segoe Fluent Icons, tab completion, command history, drag-and-drop paths, and UAC elevation. English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese.
project.processSH.stack: C# · WinUI 3 · Windows App SDK · PowerShell 7
project.taskview.title: TaskView
project.taskview.body1: A native macOS utility for viewing and managing running processes. Reads process information directly from the system using libproc, sysctl, and Darwin APIs.
project.taskview.body2: Process list with PID, name, CPU, and memory. Terminate with SIGTERM or force with SIGKILL. Search, filter, and auto-refresh.

detail.runprocess.title: RunProcess — Projects
detail.runprocess.p1: A menu bar app that wraps /bin/zsh in a polished, translucent floating window. Opens on a global hotkey (⌘⌥R by default) and hides automatically when the app loses focus, like Spotlight. Real-time output with full ANSI color support, alias-aware Tab completion, custom paths for running tools and .app bundles by name, frecency-ranked history with ⌘R fuzzy search, multi-line input with Shift+Enter, and secure sudo handling. Updates ship via Sparkle, and there's a Homebrew tap.
detail.runprocess.note: Requires macOS 12.4 or later · Apple Silicon or Intel · Also on Homebrew
detail.runprocess.p.updates: Updates are delivered through Sparkle and cryptographically signed before installation — check manually with ⌘U or enable daily background checks. Install from the Releases page, or via Homebrew: brew tap CaoHaoran-Dev/apptap, brew trust CaoHaoran-Dev/apptap, brew install runprocess. The app isn't notarized, so the first launch may need Open Anyway in Privacy & Security.
detail.runprocess.p.run: Output streams in real time through Process and Pipe, with ANSI colors rendered properly — git status, ls -G, grep --color all show up as intended. Tab completion covers aliases, command history, system commands, and file paths. History is ranked by frecency (frequency × recency) and searchable with ⌘R fuzzy matching. Aliases let you define short names like gs for git status.
detail.runprocess.p.files: Drag files in from Finder to insert their full paths, properly escaped. Handy for anything that takes a path as an argument. Settings → Paths also lets you add folders like /Applications or ~/bin, so command-line tools found there can be run by name and .app bundles can be launched by name — typing keynote opens Keynote.
detail.runprocess.p.sudo: When a command needs elevated privileges, RunProcess prompts for the password and uses it only in memory during execution. It's never stored or logged — every sudo command asks again. A "Default Sudo" option can lock the main window into run-as-root mode.
detail.runprocess.p.appearance: Three modes — None, Frosted Glass, and Liquid Glass (macOS 26+) — let the window match whatever the rest of your screen is doing. None is a solid system window background. Frosted Glass uses NSVisualEffectView blur and is the default on macOS 15 and earlier. Liquid Glass is the native macOS 26 material, default there and hidden on systems that don't support it. The chosen style applies to the main window, Settings, Help, About, and the sudo dialog.
detail.runprocess.p.session: By default, each window is its own shell — cd and export are lost after each command. Session mode keeps a long-running zsh process alive within a window, so cd and export persist across commands, closer to a real terminal. It only affects newly opened windows, and the window title shows RunProcess - Session — <current directory>. Multiple windows stay fully isolated from each other.
detail.runprocess.p.demo: RunProcess is also available in the browser.
detail.processSH.title: ProcessSH — Projects
detail.processSH.p1: A Windows port of RunProcess. A lightweight PowerShell 7 launcher with an acrylic interface, system tray integration, and a global hotkey. Built with C# and WinUI 3.
detail.processSH.p.features: Execute any PowerShell command with real-time output. Tab completion for commands, history, and file paths. Command history with ↑ and ↓. Drag files from Explorer to insert escaped paths. Run as administrator with a UAC prompt.
detail.processSH.p.appearance: Native Windows Acrylic backdrop for a translucent, modern look. The window floats at the bottom-left corner of the screen, inspired by Spotlight on macOS. Segoe Fluent Icons throughout.
detail.processSH.p.hotkey: Ctrl+Alt+R shows or hides the window globally. The default uses Ctrl+Alt instead of Ctrl+Win because Windows reserves many Win key combinations, and RegisterHotKey cannot reliably capture them. Customizable in Settings.
detail.processSH.p.tray: Lives in the system tray, no taskbar icon. Closing the main window hides it rather than exiting. To quit, use Tray → Quit.
detail.processSH.p.lang: English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese. Switch at runtime in Settings → Language.
detail.swiftZip.title: Swift Zip Manager — Projects
detail.swiftZip.p1: An archive tool that feels like it belongs on the Mac. Built with Swift and SwiftUI, designed to stay out of the way.
detail.swiftZip.p.formats: ZIP, TAR, GZ, 7Z, and RAR. Encrypted archives are supported. The app checks for the 7zz and RAR command-line tools on first launch and installs them in one click if they're missing.
detail.swiftZip.p.browsing: Open an archive without unpacking it. Contents show up in List or Grid view, whichever suits the archive better. Drag files in from Finder to add them. Extract or delete individual entries without touching the rest.
detail.swiftZip.p.interface: Built entirely in SwiftUI. Native window controls, native menus, native everything. Supports multiple languages. Auto-updates check through the GitHub API.
detail.swiftZip.p.devMode: A hidden mode for the workflows most people never need — the ones I do. Enable it if you know why you'd want it.
detail.taskview.title: TaskView — Projects
detail.taskview.p1: A native macOS utility for viewing and managing running processes. Built with SwiftUI, using libproc, sysctl, and Darwin APIs to read process information directly from the system.
detail.taskview.p.features1: Process list with PID, name, CPU, and memory. Select a process to see details: user, start time, status, path, and parent PID. Terminate with SIGTERM, or force with SIGKILL.
detail.taskview.p.features2: Search and filter to find what you need. Auto-refresh keeps the list current.
detail.taskview.p.issues: This is an alpha. Some user processes show a blank name, and some show Unix Time Zero as their start time. System processes like kernel_task and WindowServer cannot be terminated.
detail.webdemo.title: Process WebHub — Projects
detail.webdemo.tagline: RunProcess and ProcessSH, in your browser.
detail.webdemo.p1: A static, multi-page site that hosts browser demos for both native apps: RunProcess for macOS and ProcessSH for Windows. Pure HTML, CSS, and JavaScript — no frameworks, no build tools, no backend.
detail.webdemo.p.desktop: A landing page lets you pick a platform, then drops you into a working recreation of that desktop. macOS traffic lights and menu bar, or the Windows taskbar and system tray — all in pure CSS and web fonts. Windows are fully draggable via Pointer Events (mouse, trackpad, and touch), and expand smoothly in height as output appears, just like the native apps.
detail.webdemo.p.shell: A set of preset commands returns mock output with ANSI-like formatting. Nothing is executed on your machine — every response is hardcoded, including the sudo and UAC prompts, which are visual only.
detail.webdemo.p.languages: Full localization for English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese, loaded at runtime from JSON. Switch anytime without a page reload.
detail.webdemo.p.why: Pick from 8 built-in gradient wallpapers or import your own image (stored locally in localStorage). Switch window materials: Frosted Glass and Liquid Glass for RunProcess, Mica, Acrylic, and Solid for ProcessSH. Drag windows around, run simulated commands, and see how both interfaces behave without installing anything.
detail.webdemo.p.limits: Commands are simulated only. Sudo and admin mode are visual. Imported wallpapers are stored as Data URLs in localStorage, which browsers typically cap around 5 MB. Liquid Glass refraction in RunProcess needs SVG displacement maps, supported only in Chromium-based browsers — Safari and Firefox fall back to a frosted glass effect.
